articles.title: Machine-Learning Geographic Sampling Frames Underrepresent People on the Move in Fragile Settings
articles.authors: Andrea Carlomaria Caflisch, Daniel Masterson, Stephen Daniel O'Connell, Ettan Patel, Julia Smith Omomo
articles.abstract: Political science research often studies difficult-to-locate populations: internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, migrants, and others who move during war, disaster, or crisis. We compare machine-learning (ML)-generated building footprints against high-resolution satellite imagery for constructing sampling frames. In displacement- affected communities in Iraq, 15.5% of ML points were invalid or duplicated, and manual additions constituted 19% of the final hybrid frame. Manual additions reached 10.2 percentage points more IDPs in rural communities and 10.1 more returnees in urban areas. We attribute differences to two mechanisms: temporary and informal shelters are harder for ML algorithms to detect, while post-bombardment reconstruction can create structures absent from the imagery underlying ML frames. ML-only frames produce systematic coverage error, and targeted satellite validation can reduce it.

articles.title: Workplace Mental Health and Psychological Safety: A Systematic Review of Interventions and Outcomes
articles.abstract: Background. Workplace mental health and psychological safety are critical determinants of employee wellbeing, organizational performance, and public health. Despite growing recognition of their importance, evidence on effective interventions across occupational sectors remains fragmented, and the moderating role of psychosocial safety climate (PSC) is underexplored in existing syntheses. Objective. This systematic review synthesizes global evidence on individual- and organizational-level workplace mental health interventions, with particular attention to psychological safety climate as a moderating construct and the differential effectiveness of universal versus targeted delivery models. Methods. A comprehensive, PRISMA 2020-compliant search was conducted across PubMed and Google Scholar databases, covering publications from 2011 to 2026. Ninety-seven records were identified; following removal of four duplicates, 93 deduplicated records were retained, encompassing systematic reviews, meta-analyses, umbrella reviews, and qualitative syntheses. Quality appraisal employed ROBINS-I, QATQS, AXIS, Downs and Black, GRADE, and EPHPP tools. Results. Individual-level digital interventions demonstrated the strongest measurable short-term effects: mindfulness-based eHealth programs (Hedge’s g = 0.60) outperformed cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT; g = 0.15) and stress management programs (g = 0.17). Web-based interventions improved psychological wellbeing (g = 0.37) and work effectiveness (g = 0.25), with effects sustained at follow-up (g = 0.23). Targeted delivery yielded markedly larger effects for stress management (g = 0.64–0.69) compared to universal delivery (g = 0.00). Universal CBT reduced depression across the general workforce (SMD = 0.16). Manager training significantly increased mental health knowledge (SMD = 0.73). Among healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic, pooled disorder prevalence reached 36% for depression, 37% for PTSD, 27% for stress, 47% for anxiety, and 49% for insomnia. Organizational-level interventions showed mixed results with high heterogeneity. Conclusions. Effective workplace mental health promotion requires multi-layered strategies that combine scalable digital tools with organizational structural changes and manager capability building. Future research should prioritize longitudinal designs, under-represented worker populations, cost-effectiveness analyses, and the integration of PSC measurement into intervention frameworks.

articles.title: Resilient Citizens in Resilient Societies: The Determinants of Individuals’ Resilience
articles.abstract: Structural change and recurrent crises are causing major disruptions to societies and citizens. There- fore, both policy-makers and scientists widely encourage strengthening individuals’ resilience. But social science resilience-literature is often criticized for ambivalent conceptualization and limited policy-applicability. We therefore aim at identifying the determinants of individuals’ resilience while addressing these shortcomings. Our theoretical framework conceptualizes resilience in terms of empirically testable life-course capitals that help individuals maintain desired outcomes by meeting changed resource-needs and reduced resource-access during disturbances. These life-course capitals include not only an individual’s economic and human capital, but also their social capital (from meso-level social networks) and “institutional capital” (support from macro-level public institutions). As such these capitals are multi-dimensional, multi-level, and interacting. Our empirical analysis employs multi-level regression models using longitudinal individual-level (n=16,071) and country-level data across 23 European countries during the COVID-19 pandemic. We find all life-course capital variables – lower economic arrears, savings, housing insecurity, education, health, social inclusion, public social expenditure, and government effectiveness – are positively associated with individual resilience. Social inclusion matters most, followed by health. We also find substitution-effects between life-course capitals. Life-course capitals explain a total of 22% of the resilience-variance – explain- ing around 45% of the between-country(-group) variance (1-2% of the total variance), 36% of the between-individual variance (62%), and practically no within-individual resilience-variance (37%). Associations are rather stable across country-groups, but in Southern Europe social inclusion, education, and institutional capital matter slightly more. These findings suggest that a multi-dimensional policy approach – prioritizing social inclusion and public health while considering country-specific conditions – can be promising.

articles.title: Fertility, Affiliation Transmission, and Religious Reproduction in Germany
articles.abstract: Religious groups reproduce across generations through childbearing and the transmission of affiliation. I examine how these processes jointly shape religious composition in Germany. A pseudo-prospective design combines repeated cross-sectional surveys of women’s affiliation and fertility with retrospective information on maternal affiliation and adult offspring affiliations from the German Socio-Economic Panel. I reconstruct five-group distributions for women born in 1931-1950 and their offspring, including childless women in the starting population. Under the assumptions linking these sources, fertility differences modify but do not reverse the generational redistribution associated with affiliation transmission. Catholic point estimates indicate partial fertility compensation for transmission losses, whereas Protestant fertility provides little compensation. Lower fertility moderates but does not eliminate unaffiliated gains. Across maternal cohorts, the unaffiliated generational gap narrows as the maternal share rises toward a comparatively stable reconstructed offspring share. Unaffiliated mothers also account for a growing share of unaffiliated offspring. A conditional reconstruction for women born in 1951-1970 yields the same directions in the point estimates under fixed transmission probabilities. The findings quantify the limited extent of fertility compensation in the reconstructed religious reproduction of these cohorts.

articles.title: Immigrant wages are lower in immigrant-dense areas, and the limited-English differential is mostly occupational: metropolitan Philadelphia, 2012–2024

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Immigrants who speak limited English earn less than those who speak it well. On the protective view of residential concentration, that differential should be smaller where immigrants are concentrated, because concentration supplies employers and customers who do not require English. On the isolation view it should be larger. This study tests both views in metropolitan Philadelphia, a former gateway whose immigrant population has grown again, with American Community Survey microdata for 2012 to 2024 and a two-level model of 7,355 foreign-born workers in 48 Public Use Microdata Areas. Hourly wages are about 8 percent lower per standard deviation of area immigrant density for foreign-born workers who speak English well and about 3 percent lower, an estimate not distinguishable from zero, for those who speak it poorly. Native-born workers in the same areas show a gradient of 2 percent, so most of the difference is specific to immigrants. The interaction between density and limited English is 0.049 (standard error 0.029) and disappears once occupation is held constant. The limited-English differential is 21 percent overall and 9 percent within an occupation, so most of it is associated with the occupations limited-English workers hold. An exploratory measure of the density of the worker’s own home language gives a positive interaction of 0.046 (0.022), driven by lower wages for proficient workers rather than higher wages for limited-English workers, and the same specification in the New York metropolitan area gives 0.045 (0.009). Higher earners move from the city to the suburbs.

articles.title: List and Sequential Attention
articles.abstract: This paper studies stochastic choice when both availability and presentation order may vary across choice problems. We characterize a fixed-list sequential attention model for menu choice and a sequential attention model with a common continuation profile for list choice. In the list domain, we further show that, holding preferences fixed, more persistent attention shifts choice probability toward more preferred alternatives.

articles.title: AI Systems for Filmmaking: A Survey of HCI Research from a Labor-Centered Perspective
articles.authors: YUYING TANG, Lin Gao, Haotian Li, Baiqiao Zhang, Rebecca Fiebrink, Sebastian Deterding, Xiaojuan Ma, Huamin Qu
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence is integrated into filmmaking and has attracted attention in human-computer interaction (HCI). Existing studies have primarily characterized AI systems for filmmaking by their capabilities and supported tasks, with limited attention to the organisation of filmmaking labor during system use. We review 31 HCI system papers and develop a three-layer taxonomy of labor sites, labor types, and human-AI allocation, examining where AI systems are positioned, what types of labor are involved during system use, and how those labor types are allocated between humans and AI. Our analysis reveals a concentration on individual below-the-line contexts, increasing attention to structural and meaning-making labor beyond execution, comparatively limited relational labor, and substantial variation in human-AI allocation across labor types. We further identify opportunities for the design and evaluation of AI systems that account for the broader organization of filmmaking labor. This review provides a labor-centered taxonomy for synthesizing AI systems for filmmaking and a basis for examining how AI may become involved in broader organizations of creative labor.

articles.title: Who Speaks When the Chatbot Answers? Generative AI as Institutional Speech
articles.authors: Bibhor Acharya, Sandesh Gupta, Himani Moktan
articles.abstract: When a branded chatbot answers a customer, the reply is often taken as the institution speaking. This paper treats that uptake as a media and communication problem rather than as a model-accuracy problem alone. Using Erving Goffman’s account of footing—the gap between who animates an utterance and who stands as its principal—and Austin and Searle’s account of commitments as speech acts, we read the British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal decision in Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024 BCCRT 149) as a public episode of institutional speech gone wrong. A website chatbot told Jake Moffatt that a bereavement fare could be claimed retroactively within ninety days; a different page on the same site, and later human staff, denied that path. Air Canada argued it should not be held liable for the chatbot; the tribunal disagreed and ordered damages. The case lets us follow authorization, utterance, uptake, contested repair, and the failed attempt to split the animator from the principal. While systematic reviews of AI disadvantages map privacy, displacement, and bias at a macroeconomic scale, they leave open this micro-communicative surface where an institution’s name is attached to a fluent reply. We argue that handoff to a named human is part of the speech act when commitment is at stake, not an optional engineering fallback.

articles.title: Consumer-level Virtual Reality Applications and Users' Wellbeing: The Role of Problematic Use, Social Support, Harassment, and the Medium's Affordances
articles.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) applications are increasingly adopted by consumers for gaming, social interaction, and other purposes, raising questions about their impact on users' wellbeing. Against this backdrop, this study explores the associations between experiences of problematic use, social support, and harassment during the use of consumer-level VR applications and users' wellbeing-related variables, as well as how the affordances of these applications may facilitate each of these mechanisms. We conducted a pre-registered online survey (N = 717) with VR users of a diverse range of applications. Results showed that perceived social support obtained in VR environments was a positive predictor of both wellbeing and life satisfaction, while harassment was a negative predictor of life satisfaction. While a bivariate correlation existed between screen time and users' wellbeing, it disappeared once these experiential variables were accounted for, suggesting that what happens during VR use matters more than how long it lasts. Social presence and embodiment while using VR were positively associated with problematic use, social support, and (social presence only) harassment, while moderation affordances were positively associated with social support. Loot boxes emerged as a robust predictor of problematic use, extending gambling-adjacent reward mechanics documented in conventional gaming to VR specifically. These findings provide a first quantitative, integrated approach to factors that have so far been studied mainly from a qualitative standpoint or in isolation, supporting a shift away from dose-response models of VR's effects toward affordance- and mechanism-based frameworks.

articles.title: The Ranma ½ Effect: Why the Same Aggression Does Not Look Equally Dangerous
articles.abstract: This paper develops the ‘Ranma ½ Effect,’ a testable theoretical account of why identical or substantively similar aggressive behavior may be perceived as more or less dangerous depending on the social configuration in which it occurs. The discussion begins with recurring forms of comic punishment in Japanese popular culture, including Ranma 1/2, and connects them to existing research on humor, gender, intimate partner violence, anger expression, leadership, organizational silence, and employee voice. Prior findings are mixed: aggression toward male targets is sometimes judged as less serious, whereas women who express anger in professional settings can be evaluated more negatively than men. Rather than treating these findings as contradictory, this paper argues that perceived dangerousness is configuration-dependent. Gender, age, status, experience, physical formidability, prior reputation, relational context, cultural framing, and observer norms jointly shape whether an act is interpreted as aggression, strictness, guidance, punishment, or simply “the way that person is.” Two workplace observations are used as theory-generating illustrations. In one setting, strong public corrective behavior by a highly competent and positively regarded manager coexisted with favorable evaluations of competence and leadership. In another, a comparatively young manager coordinated older, experienced workers without relying on anger as a primary control resource. These observations are used to construct a counterfactual comparison in which the conduct is held constant while the actor-target configuration is altered, providing a basis for future vignette experiments. The central argument is that social judgments of aggression are shaped not only by what is done, but also by who does it to whom and under what relational and cultural conditions. Such perceptual differences may affect third-party intervention, corrective feedback, and the continued use or normalization of aggressive managerial behavior. The danger of the Ranma ½ Effect lies not only in making aggression acceptable, but in making aggression less recognizable as aggression.

articles.title: Algorithmic Serendipity, Excessive Scrolling, and Creative Thinking in Short-Form Video Consumption: A Theoretical Review.
articles.abstract: Short form videos from different apps have become popular ways for entertainment and relaxation. It has transformed digital media consumption through personalized recommendations and rapid content delivery. This theoretical review examines the relationship between algorithmic serendipity, excessive scrolling and creativity in short-form video consumption. This review proposes two interconnected pathways. One suggests that unexpected and relevant algorithmic recommendation may generate curiosity and anticipation of future discoveries encouraging continuous scrolling. Second path suggests that exposure to diverse information, ideas and perspectives may support creative thinking, at the same time, prolonged exposure and continuous scrolling reduces sustained attention and deeper cognitive processing required for creativity. Thus, algorithmic serendipity may represent double edge process. The review provides a theoretical basis for future empirical research examining the conditions under which algorithmic created video consumption may support or hinder creative thinking.

articles.title: The Counter Monster: How Organizational Pressure Is Eaten and Converted into Knowledge, External Value, and Persistence
articles.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical model explaining why organizational pressure does not always produce silence, compliance, or exit. Existing research on employee voice, organizational silence, whistleblowing, abusive supervision, job embeddedness, and resilience has extensively examined how employees respond to unfavorable organizational conditions. Less attention, however, has been paid to situations in which pressure itself becomes material for observation, documentation, comparison, theorization, and external value creation, and in which that value subsequently feeds back into the actor’s capacity to remain autonomous from internal organizational evaluation. The paper introduces the concept of the Counter Monster and identifies Pressure-Eating as its core mechanism. Pressure-Eating refers to the process through which organizational pressure is experienced not only as psychological or occupational loss but also as information containing contradictions, repetitions, institutional responses, and changes in organizational explanations that can later be analyzed. The concept does not imply that pressure becomes harmless. Rather, damage and information may coexist. The paper further develops Cross-Domain Incentive Inversion to describe situations in which an event carrying negative value within the organization acquires different value in external domains such as research, professional practice, legal processes, or external networks. When this conversion occurs, pressure intended or experienced as increasing the cost of staying may simultaneously generate new observational or knowledge value. This possibility is conceptualized as the Exit Pressure Paradox. The recursive connection among organizational pressure, Pressure-Eating, knowledge production, external value, reduced dependence on internal evaluation, persistence, and further organizational responses is theorized as the Counter Loop. The Counter Monster is treated not as a stable personality type but as an actor-state emerging from the interaction of resilience, autonomy, analytical capacity, externalization capacity, and the availability of external value arenas. Generative AI is positioned not as the cause of the Counter Monster but as an external cognitive medium that can reduce the costs of documentation, comparison, literature connection, drafting, translation, and externalization. Finally, the paper proposes the Boring Organization Principle: organizations are more likely to weaken the Counter Loop by maintaining fair procedures, explainable decisions, revisability, and ordinary treatment than by escalating exceptional control. The theory does not celebrate adversity or harassment; it argues instead that organizations cannot fully control the meaning and downstream value of the pressure they impose.

articles.title: An Exploratory Study On The Presentation Of News On Select Print Media Using Framing Analysis
articles.abstract: This study explores the presentation and framing of the Koodankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KKNPP) protest in two leading English-language newspapers in Tamil Nadu, The Hindu and The New Indian Express. The study examines how mainstream print media selected, emphasized, and presented different dimensions of the protest and how these framing patterns contributed to the construction of public discourse. A comparative content analysis was conducted on news reports published during September 2012, focusing on coverage of the KKNPP protest in the Tirunelveli and Chennai editions of the selected newspapers. Framing theory, particularly the conceptual framework associated with Erving Goffman and Robert Entman, was employed to identify and analyze dominant, causes, and definitions frames. The study examined frames including de-legitimizing, legitimizing, injustice, sympathy, contextual, state/court reinforcement, human rights violations, freedom of expression, targeting marginalized groups, external influence, environmental considerations, unrest, uprising, protest, conspiracy, and chaos. The findings indicate differences between the two newspapers in several framing categories. Significant differences were observed in selected frames, including de-legitimizing, sympathy, contextual, protest, conspiracy, and chaos, while other frames showed comparatively limited differences. The study concludes that mainstream print media coverage of the KKNPP protest was not uniform and that the framing of the issue shifted across different stages of the protest, particularly from state/court reinforcement towards human rights and freedom-of-expression perspectives. The findings highlight the importance of examining news selection, emphasis, and framing in understanding the construction of media narratives surrounding social movements and public controversies.

articles.title: Cricket as Entertainment and Politics in India
articles.authors: Ramprasath P S, Dr. Manikkam K
articles.abstract: Cricket in India is not a sport; it is part of entertainment and politics. This study considers the working of cricket both as enjoyment and as a political tool. It shows how cricket has moved from a colonial sport to a powerful platform for image-making, branding, and international relations with the help of media and prominent people. The following study adopts a qualitative approach by analysing books, interviews, and content on three broad issues: the use of cricket as a prop by politicians, especially through the IPL, for image building; increased participation through fantasy leagues and digital platforms; and cricket as something more than just a game. Strong institutions, like the BCCI, are found instrumental in connecting cricket to politics. Media frames people's interpretation of cricket and often presents it as an icon of wealth, youth, and development while masking several aspects of political and commercial influence over cricket. The study further reveals that caste, nepotism, and family relationships are also linked with the interpretation of cricket as entertainment. The present research argues that cricket is not merely a source of entertainment but also a political gadget. It is a site where debates and contests over national identity, social cohesion, and political authority are being conducted. The implications of the study are immense on media, culture, and sports management.

articles.title: From Public Objection to Standing and Back: Mediated Public Authorization
articles.abstract: How can practices that sustain a public concern change who is entitled to pursue it? This article develops Mediated Public Authorization, a framework connecting public persistence with practical standing. It specifies two contingent mechanisms: mediated objections become usable grounds for allocating standing, and implemented allocations enter production practices that reorganise subsequent questioning. Public renewal depends on participants using those arrangements. A hypothetical service controversy shows how these connections differ from exposure, source visibility, favourable reception and administrative change alone. Drawing on research on media standing, mediated political interaction, representation and publicness, the framework traces participant-linked claim passages and distinguishes entitlements from obligations to answer. It proposes conditional expectations about contextual retrieval, evidentiary transmission, entitlement reproduction and renewed questioning. It also specifies a pathway to institutional adaptation and a benchmark for inequality in new entitlement grants. MPA examines how a concern can remain publicly contestable as its speakers, constituencies and routes of pursuit change.

articles.title: The Quiet Male: Exploring Silence and Masculinity in Jaggi (2022)
articles.abstract: This investigation concerns that the story of the film revolves around the inferiority and marginalization of the protagonist, Jaggi (2022), whose failure to execute heterosexual virility is a direct opposition to the local organization of hegemonic masculinity of physical toughness, aggressiveness, and unchallenged sexual potency (Naahar, 2024). The movie, which unfolds the story of a rural schoolboy that is victimized by the harassment of unstoppable bullies and was labeled a homosexual due to his inability to procreate, is interpreted as the vivid depiction of violence required to realize an idealized masculinity. The paper focuses on the patriarchal enforcing of the gender order by the hegemonic men characters of the movie the bullies and the patriarch family of Jaggi (2022) through the use of violence and cultural exclusion. Their violent and noisy shows are contrasted with the silent suffering of Jaggi (2022) to remind us of the disciplining nature of hegemonic masculinity in imposing gender obedience on men. This deadly aspect of this repressive gender regime is demonstrated by the fateful choice that Jaggi (2022) made in the end. Jaggi (2022) is therefore an interesting case study of the way that hegemonic masculinity is perpetuated via the discursive and affective act of erasing other forms of masculinity and in this regard, silence becomes a loquid signifier of systemic violence.

articles.title: Femme Fatale in Tamil Cinema: An Analysis of Varalaxmi Sarathkumar’s Antagonistic Characterization in Sarkar (2018) and Sandakozhi 2 (2018)
articles.abstract: Feminist film theory and the concept of femme fatale have been adopted as the theoretical underpinning of this study. The present study aims to understand and explore the concept of femme fatale and its manifestation through the female antagonists in the movies Sarkar and Sandakozhi 2. Generally, women in Tamil cinema have had little scope as antagonists, being relegated to supporting and romantic interests within patriarchal narratives. Recent Tamil cinema has, however, started to offer more nuanced and complex female antagonists who break away from traditional gender constructs. The present study aims to explore and understand the concept of femme fatale and its manifestation through the female antagonists in the movies Sarkar (2018) and Sandakozhi 2 (2018) portrayed by Varalaxmi Sarathkumar. The present study aims to understand and explore how the concept of femme fatale is represented in the movies Sarkar and Sandakozhi 2.

articles.title: The 128 Paths to Victory - Swing State Math in the U.S. Presidential Elections
articles.authors: N. Asger Mortensen, Joel D. Cox
articles.abstract: In U.S. presidential elections, outcomes are often predictable in most states, with variability primarily introduced by a small number of "swing states". While the specific swing states can fluctuate from one election cycle to the next, they collectively play a critical role in determining the overall result. In the 2024 election, seven key swing states contribute a total of 93 delegates to the electoral college. Without considering mutual correlations, each of the 128 potential electoral outcomes has an equal probability of approximately 0.8%. Due to an uneven distribution of "safe" delegates (219 Republican and 226 Democrat), the Democratic candidate holds a slight statistical advantage. Analysing all possible outcomes for the 2024 election suggests an estimated 55% probability for a Democratic win, compared to 42% for a Republican victory. The odds of a tie are approximately 2.3%, while the likelihood of either party achieving a clean sweep of all swing states is 0.8%. A detailed analysis of the 128 possible election outcomes reinforces the widely held view that securing Pennsylvania is crucial to electoral success. Notably, in 4\% of all possible scenarios, victory is achieved by the narrowest possible margin, and in every such case, it hinges on winning Pennsylvania.

articles.title: "I don't give a shit anymore" – Future-Oriented Career Agency and Precarity at the Postdoc Stage
articles.authors: Julian Hamann, Kathia Serrano Velarde, Tim Fenkner, Jonas Gottschalk-Rayling, Sven Boniger, Michi Hügel
articles.abstract: This paper examines how postdoctoral researchers navigate precarious employment conditions and claim career agency during an uncertain career stage. Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative interview panel of 35 postdocs from particle physics and modern history, the study distinguishes between two forms of agency: empowered strategizing and restricted drifting. Strategizing postdocs actively align short- to mid-term career goals with opportunities arising from fixed-term contracts and grant funding cycles, while drifting postdocs prioritize present research activities over long-term planning. Through in-depth interviews conducted in three waves, the analysis reveals how temporal horizons are compressed by the cyclical nature of academic recruitment and funding. The findings highlight the dynamic interplay between structural constraints and different forms of individual agency. This work contributes a processual perspective on career agency and precarity and adds to career research and studies of precarious working conditions.

articles.title: Measuring the impact of area-based early years support in Wales on children’s social care: Preliminary findings
articles.authors: Meng Le Zhang, Martin Elliott, Gareth Griffith, Sally Holland
articles.abstract: Flying Start is an area-based intervention which offers support for families with children under four living in disadvantaged areas in Wales. This study uses a quasi-experiment (Regression Discontinuity Design) and administrative data on children born in Wales between 2012 and 2017 (n = 126,705) to measure the impact of Flying Start eligibility on children’s social care at age 4/5. We find that Flying Start reduces rates of children with care and support plans and children looked after. These effects are stronger for male infants and mothers who were 21 or younger at childbirth. However, we find no effects on child protection.

articles.title: Answering without disclosing: How officials under scrutiny compress what they say

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: How do organisational actors withhold information while continuing to answer under scrutiny? Research on organisational silence has largely treated withholding as a question of whether actors speak. This article examines variation within speech through 1 781 question-and-answer exchanges from 102 recorded interview encounters with senior officials in prison health governance across three studies conducted between 2016 and 2023. Narrative absence was coded across six features and response timing was derived from audio and validated against blinded listener judgements. Higher narrative absence was associated with substantially shorter answers within encounters, and this association held across all robustness checks. Changes in response onset were much smaller, while pausing supported no independent association, and the automated measure of fillers and repairs failed validation. The findings identify controlled compression as a response form through which disclosure contracts while interactional responsiveness continues. Separating responsiveness from disclosure matters because organisational accountability is routinely assessed through visible responsiveness even though meaningful accountability depends on disclosure. An actor may therefore satisfy every observable requirement of cooperation while narrowing what is made available. The article shows that where speaking is expected, withholding does not cease but relocates into the answers themselves.

articles.title: Doubly Preferential: The Treatment of Contested Experts in News Media
articles.authors: François Claveau, Jacob Hamel-Mottiez, Léon Gatien, Olivier Santerre
articles.abstract: This article contributes to the characterization of media bias by analyzing how Canadian news media select and contextualize messages originating from think tanks, an influential yet ideologically marked form of expertise. Drawing on a large media corpus (2017–2021), this article shows that Canadian journalists make relatively limited use of textual indicators of credibility, but that these indicators systematically reflect the ideological preferences already evident in their source selection. Think tanks that are more frequently solicited thus benefit from more favorable contextualization, corroborating the hypothesis of a doubly preferential treatment. The study concludes by discussing the normative implications of these practices for journalistic standards, such as impartiality, in the face of contested expertise.

articles.title: Hate speech against scientists can backfire – but so can counterspeech: Evidence from a four-country experiment
articles.abstract: Hate speech against scientists can harm their well-being and undermine knowledge-based societies, and counterspeech by bystanders is often proposed as a remedy. But comparative evidence on how bystanders perceive hate speech targeting scientists and on whether counterspeech helps is lacking. In a preregistered experiment with quota samples weighted to national population margins from Denmark, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States (N = 2,769), participants saw a fictitious social media post by a scientist either alone, with a hateful comment, or with a hateful comment plus a counterspeech reply. Hate speech backfired: Participants rated the scientist’s post more positively in both comment conditions. Counterspeech had mixed effects: It increased participants’ intentions to speak up themselves, but in Germany and the United Kingdom it made the hateful comment appear more acceptable. Our findings advance research on attacks against epistemic authorities and demonstrate the value of comparative, multi-outcome designs.

articles.title: Empathy-Related Traits and Domain-Specific Self-Rated Creativity: Indirect Associations Through Five C-PETS Dimensions
articles.abstract: This study examined statistical indirect associations between empathy-related traits and domain-specific self-rated creativity through five dimensions of the Creative Personality and Thinking Styles Scale (C-PETS). An online survey of 359 North American adults assessed Perspective Taking (PT), Fantasy (FS), and Empathic Concern (EC), the five C-PETS dimensions, and five domains of the Kaufman Domains of Creativity Scale (K-DOCS). Parallel multiple mediation models were estimated using 10,000 bootstrap samples and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Significant total indirect effects were found for PT across all five K-DOCS domains, for FS across four domains, and for EC only for Self/Everyday creativity. After correction, significant specific indirect effects were limited to Challenge-Seeking (CS) pathways from PT and FS to all five K-DOCS domains. Because the data were cross-sectional and based on self-report, these results do not establish causal mediation. Instead, they indicate that challenge-seeking is a robust conditional statistical link between perspective-related empathy traits and domain-specific self-rated creativity.

articles.title: From Public Dominance to Private Expansion: Changes in Hospital Infrastructure in Spain (1986–2018)

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: In many countries, the growth of the private hospital sector coincides with a decline in beds per inhabitant. Spain is no exception, showing one of the lowest relative bed provisions in the EU. This study offers an exploratory analysis of the evolution of private hospital bed provision in Spain and its Autonomous Communities between 1986 and 2018. Using historical hospital catalogs from the Ministry of Health, we conducted graphical and cluster analyses to examine trends and classify regions by the share of private hospital beds. Results indicate a national trend toward fewer beds and a growing presence of the private, mainly for-profit, sector, with notable regional differences such as the Catalan model. This research provides comparative and long-term evidence on structural changes in Spain’s hospital system.

articles.title: “AI” as gaslighting – Considering the affordances of stochastic generative systems in relation to anthropo-centered epistemic operations
articles.abstract: This paper mobilizes the notion of ‘AI’ as a carcinogen, as developed by Berman, to then inquire and analyze what is the possible human impact that results from the democratization of the use of Large Language Models and Generative Pretrained Transformers, from the perspective of how epistemic frameworks are mobilized as a core component of sociability. It then advances the proposal that we understand ‘AI’ as a case of the ‘Thomas Theorem’, and that, as such, LLMs and GPTs can effectively operate as systems of non-targeted, non-intentional, gaslighting. From that approach, the paper follows up with a materially-grounded analysis of how the operations performed on data for the creation and usage of LLMs and GPTs mean that these technologies have the affordance of being episteme-fixative, and that such an affordance (as defined here) is specific to these technologies, in a way that allows for non-essentialist and non-deterministic analysis that considers both changes and continuities in both media systems and our everyday engagement with them. It concludes by suggesting venues of inquiry that are made easier by the previous conclusions, and returns to capitalism’s uptake of technology, rather than to any immanent aspect of technology, as a central aspect to consider in evaluating the epistemic harms that might come out of these affordances.

articles.title: Using large-scale supermarket transaction data to understand the environmental sustainability and healthiness of food and drink purchases. Policy Insights from the FIO Food Project.
articles.authors: Emma Wilkins, Mark Alan Green, Mark Gilthorpe, Alice Kininmonth, Alexandra Johnstone, Michelle Morris
articles.abstract: A policy brief summarising recommendations for policy from FIO Food work package 2, which uses large-scale retail transaction data to understand the environmental sustainability and healthiness of food and drink purchases.

articles.title: Occupational class inequality in non-monetary job quality in Europe, 1995-2024
articles.abstract: Occupational class is central to research on inequality, but we have limited knowledge about how it structures non-monetary job quality across countries and over time. We examine four dimensions of job quality—autonomy, physical working conditions, work intensity, and work time quality—across eight occupational classes in 14 European countries from 1995 to 2024, using the European Working Conditions Survey. We compare class profiles over time, decompose variation into within- and between-class components, and benchmark occupational class against country, country-year, and income. Most variation in job quality is within occupational classes, but gradients remain pronounced for physical working conditions and autonomy, while work intensity is only weakly structured by class. Cross-national differences are modest on average but substantially larger among lower-skill than higher-skill classes. Occupational class thus remains an important source of inequality in some dimensions of job quality, but captures only part of the broader variation in working conditions.

articles.title: Associations between content and engagement vary across social media communities
articles.abstract: Research on social media engagement often seeks general content features that are associated with online success. However, social media platforms contain communities with different audiences, topics, and norms, and the same features may have different associations with engagement within different communities. This research considers 1,078,044 items from 587 communities in five corpora spanning Reddit, Stack Exchange, X, and YouTube. For each corpus, negativity, moralization, arousal, and in-group versus out-group language were measured. Their relationships with engagement were compared using multilevel models imposing one within-community slope per feature with models allowing slopes to vary across communities. Varying-slope models fit the data better in all five corpora. The estimated community slopes varied substantially in magnitude and, frequently, direction. Nevertheless, the average slopes from the varying-slope models remained small. The improved fit therefore reflects heterogeneity across communities rather than stronger average associations. These findings show that a weak average association can conceal stronger but opposing associations across communities. General claims about the content associated with social media engagement need to account for the specific communities in which that content appears.

articles.title: Attribute Relevance in Conjoint Analysis
articles.abstract: Researchers often rely on conjoint analysis to understand which attributes drive respondents' decisionmaking, yet standard estimands are not designed to measure attribute relevance. We introduce a novel approach to measuring attribute relevance in conjoint analysis by drawing on causal attribution methods. Our proposed estimand, the average probability of necessary and sufficient causation (APNS), captures the probability that swapping two profiles' levels on an attribute would change a respondent's choice. We establish nonparametric identification under assumptions related to preference heterogeneity, and provide simple difference-in-means estimators that can be applied to existing conjoint data structures. Two empirical applications illustrate the method. A candidate choice experiment in Germany reveals significant preference heterogeneity that leads standard estimands to mask relevance, while under the right assumptions the APNS recovers it. By contrast, in a replication of a prominent refugee experiment, we find that assuming preference homogeneity is unproblematic for many attributes of asylum-seekers.

articles.title: BirthClim_IT: A Harmonized Municipality-Level Dataset on Fertility, Environment, and Territorial Contexts in Italy, 2003–2022
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Environmental conditions and climate change, alongside spatial heterogeneity in fertility, have received increasing attention in fertility research. However, research combining these perspectives remains limited, partly due to the lack of data linking fine spatial resolution with detailed demographic, environmental, and socioeconomic information. This is particularly relevant in Italy, where substantial spatial variation in fertility coexists with heterogeneous environmental conditions. OBJECTIVE This paper introduces BirthClim_IT, a harmonized longitudinal dataset designed to support research on fertility and its environmental and territorial contexts across Italian municipalities. The dataset description is accompanied by two empirical applications illustrating its use. METHODS The BirthClim_IT dataset combines monthly demographic information with environmental, climatic, geographic, and socioeconomic indicators for 7,896 Italian municipalities from January 2003 to December 2022. The dataset contains 126 variables, harmonized to the administrative boundaries in force on January 1, 2024. To address sparsity in monthly birth counts, we also provide a spatially aggregated version comprising 4,936 spatial units and a customizable aggregation procedure. RESULTS The dataset provides both municipality-level and aggregated data, allowing fertility patterns to be examined jointly across space and time. The two descriptive applications illustrate its use in identifying distinct environmental profiles across Italian municipalities and in examining seasonal variation in fertility and environmental conditions. CONTRIBUTION Given the growing interest in environmental dimensions of fertility and increasing attention to the spatial dimension of demographic processes, BirthClim_IT provides a new and flexible resource combining fine spatial and temporal resolution with information spanning multiple dimensions of the demographic, environmental, and socioeconomic context.

articles.title: Scrutiny, sanctions, and attacks on scholars: Public acceptance and perceived deservingness in Switzerland
articles.authors: Niels G. Mede, Julia Metag, Mike S. Schäfer
articles.abstract: Different forms of critical and hostile public engagement with science have been documented worldwide. They range from valuable scrutiny to public protests, support for funding cuts, and attacks. Whether people accept such engagement, and whether they consider it deserved, has rarely been studied with representative data. Using a preregistered, nationally representative survey from Switzerland (n = 698), we examine acceptance of public scrutiny, support for sanctions, and attacks on scholars and their perceived deservingness when scholars speak out politically. We find that acceptance follows a graded hierarchy: Most respondents accept scrutiny, fewer accept sanctions, and hardly anyone accepts attacks. Two thirds consider criticism of politically outspoken scholars deserved, whereas attacks are largely rejected, although noteworthy minorities consider them deserved. Acceptance of attacks is associated with science-related populist attitudes, right-leaning views, younger age, lower income, and active online engagement. Moreover, perceived political distance from scholars is associated with acceptance of scrutiny.

articles.title: Survivors' Perspectives and Experiences of Intimate Partner Violence Perpetrator Intervention Programs and Associated Services: A Qualitative Systematic Review
articles.abstract: This qualitative systematic review synthesises survivors’ perspectives of intimate partner violence perpetrator interventions and associated support services. Specifically, it examines how different relationship structures, such as intact, co-parenting, or separated arrangements, shape these experiences and determines which program features are perceived as supporting or compromising safety. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, electronic databases were searched for peer-reviewed literature published after 1 July 2016. Although 13 studies met the initial inclusion criteria for descriptive mapping, the final thematic synthesis integrated 11 primary sources containing the specific contextual data required for qualitative analysis. The analysis generated three main analytical themes: the intervention environment, perpetrator behaviour patterns, and the survivors’ processing journey. Findings indicate that relationship structures influence how survivors experience these interventions. While individuals navigating ongoing contact or reconciliation attempts often report transactional partner compliance driven by child-access pressures or relationship motivations, those seeking complete separation report an environment of persistent hypervigilance. Survivors report that specialised advocacy and literacy provided by partner contact services support safety by deconstructing mutual-blame frameworks and shifting self blame. Conversely, interventions are perceived as compromising safety when they rely on isolated compliance checks and operate separately from substance use and mental health services, creating a false impression of behavioural change. Ultimately, the qualitative evidence indicates that measuring progress through mere attendance alone provides a misleading indicator of risk, suggesting that future policy should prioritise coordinated communication across sectors and elevate survivor-defined safety as the key indicator of program success.

articles.title: Social media and the prevention or reduction of harmful gambling: a rapid evidence review with integrated lived experience
articles.authors: Jenny Sweetman, Liz Littlewood, Patricia Darcy, Greg Forshaw, Amanda Perry, su golder
articles.abstract: Background and aims: Research has established a clear link between social media use and harmful gambling. Existing systematic reviews highlight how social media platforms enable and normalise gambling. This rapid evidence review aimed to identify interventions using social media to prevent or reduce harmful gambling. Methods: Searches were conducted (January 2026) in MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO. Searches of grey literature searches, and backward and forward citations from included references, were also completed. Independent screening, data extraction and quality assessment was undertaken by two independent reviewers. Data were analysed using narrative synthesis methods. An expert by experience group directly informed each stage of the review process. Results: From 1138 unique records, 10 studies met our inclusion criteria (2 randomised controlled trials, 2 cohort studies, 2 mixed methods studies and 4 qualitative studies). Included studies focused on brief messages, the impact of a social media platform outage, and the use of gambling support forums. Findings highlighted the benefits and potential risks of implementing gambling harm reduction strategies on social media, the role of interaction with others, and opportunities to use social media to better understand the process of recovery from problem gambling. Discussion and Conclusions: There is some evidence that social media platforms could usefully support the reduction or prevention of harmful gambling. Further research is required, co-designed by those with lived experience to optimise engagement and impact, to better understand how online interventions can support different people and to assess the effectiveness through large high-quality randomised controlled trials.

articles.title: The Dataset of World Refugee and Asylum Policies (DWRAP): de jure asylum policy for 205 countries, 1951-2022
articles.authors: Christopher W. Blair, Guy Grossman, Jeremy Weinstein
articles.abstract: More than two-thirds of the world's refugees and asylum-seekers are hosted in the developing world, yet the national laws governing their reception have never been measured comprehensively across countries or over time. We introduce the Dataset of World Refugee and Asylum Policies (DWRAP), the most expansive coding of de jure asylum and refugee policy assembled to date. DWRAP records every national law pertinent to forcibly displaced populations in 205 countries from 1951 to 2022---951 legal instruments in all. From the text of each law, we hand-code 54 policy provisions, which we aggregate into 14 strands, five fields---access, services, livelihoods, movement, and participation---and a single index of policy liberality, released in three aggregation forms. The result is a country-year panel of 11,484 observations measuring displacement-policy liberality within and across countries over seven decades. Together, these data open the causes and consequences of refugee-policy change to global, historical analysis. They measure law rather than its enforcement---and so make the distance between the two visible and measurable.

articles.title: Resilience through Pathway Specificity for Managing Climate Shocks. A Review of Evidence from East Africa.
articles.abstract: The study systematically reviews and synthesizes 74 empirical studies from East Africa, covering Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Somaliland. Using study-level, asset-based thresholds and other complementary indicators, the findings identify that household resilience is non-linear and requires targeted, specific programming. The Pathway-Specific Resilience Framework (PSRF), which the paper validates, divides the target populations into two groups: a resource-deficient group that needs asset assistance and external safety nets (socially supported livelihood resilience pathway) and an asset-based cohort that prioritizes asset protection and market-based interventions. The study found that households with constrained resources face limitations in asset accumulation, which leave them more vulnerable to persistent poverty traps. PSRF proposes poverty graduation that balances immediate protection with long-term resilience through a sequence of protocols. The first “Protocol “A” protects resource-poor (Socially supported pathway) households to prioritize consumption, direct transfers (e.g., assets), and human capital. Once households transition to “Protocol B”, the shift is from survival assistance to access to market, finance, and index-based insurance. Additionally, the PSRF integrates other cross-cutting measures to sustain immediate gains from the protocols and prevent relapses brought by climate shocks. These include basic infrastructure like access to water, healthcare, and education; Connectivity and information such as early warning systems, transport, telecommunications, and adaptation measures including climate-smart technologies. Key words: Pathway-Specific Resilience Framework (PSRF), Drought resilience, livelihood pathways, Social protection, East Africa

articles.title: Commercial video games improve species-related knowledge, perceptions, and action
articles.authors: Katie Blake, Paul J Johnson, Diogo Veríssimo
articles.abstract: Digital media often mediates human-wildlife interactions. It is feared that overexposure to virtual animals will distort public awareness and valuation of real-world species. This is alarming given the current rate of extinction. Commercial video games have attracted much attention for their capacity to engage players with biodiversity and conservation. Yet their impact for this is unclear. We use an online experiment to explore whether this medium can improve species-related knowledge, perceptions, and actions, as well as test assumptions that digitised wildlife are favoured by players over real-world counterparts. Our findings are based on a sample of 272 players and 273 non-players of Planet Zoo, using species that feature in this title. We found that both gameplay hours and recency of playing Planet Zoo are positively linked to: more accurately identifying species’ names and conservation status; how much the species are liked; threat appraisals about the likelihood and impact of species loss; and increased donations. Players donated nearly twice as much to species protection as non-players on average (£7.16 versus £4.68), and they allocated the maximum possible donation value of £20 three times as often. Furthermore, we did not observe any detrimental outcomes for digitised wildlife on responses compared to real versions, and we found that any positive effects from experience with Planet Zoo tended to be greater for reptiles than mammals. Our findings do not support concerns that digital media necessarily has harmful implications for public engagement with biodiversity and conservation. Rather, we show that commercial video games might provide an avenue for players to better understand the natural world and take action to protect it, and they might even be particularly beneficial for less desirable taxa. We challenge more game studios to bridge the gap between virtual and real nature where appropriate, joining efforts to ensure that wildlife can also persist beyond digital spaces. We encourage more researchers to pursue this line of inquiry. Given the rapid loss of biodiversity, we cannot continue to overlook how these platforms with global reach might be leveraged to drive conservation action.

articles.title: ‘Building the Internationalist City from Below’: The Role of the Czechoslovak Industrial Cooperative “Interhelpo” in Forging Urbanity in early-Soviet Bishkek
articles.abstract: Abstract The paper explores the historical trajectory of Interhelpo, an industrial cooperative from Czechoslovakia, and its role in forging urbanization “from below” in early-Soviet town of Pishpek (now Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan). In light of scarce literature available on the success and failures of Western internationalist communes in the early Soviet period, this paper draws from intensive field work in Kyrgyzstan and understudied sources in Czech, Kyrgyz, Slovak and Russian to offer a novel, bottom-up narrative on the socialist city in Central Asia. Founded 1924 by Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, German internationalists and Ido-learners around the mountaineer and Bolshevik Rudolf Pavlovič Mareček in the Czechoslovakian town Žilina, the cooperative actively shaped urbanization in what would be become known as the capital of Soviet Kyrgyzstan. From 1925 until its liquidation during WWII, the cooperative built from scratch a whole district including the first electric power station of the city, textile and furniture factories, workshops for tailors, shoemakers and joiners, a school, a kindergarten, a tannery, a brewery as well as unique residential district. In the process, the cooperative forged an organic patchwork language referred to as spontánne esperanto to secure translocal collaboration between internationalists from Central Europe, on the one hand, and a heterogeneous mix of workers including Armenians, Kyrgyz, Dungans, Uygurs, Uzbeks, Russians and Ukrainians, on the other. Transcending a purely historical analysis, the paper ultimately turns to the urban landscape of present-day Bishkek. There it argues that while the district built by Interhelpo corresponds today to an exiled site dislocated by the hegemonic ethno-national memory regime, its materiality harbors relicts of another future capable of mobilizing alternative narratives on the city and her socialist and multi-ethnic past.

articles.title: Research dataset sharing and ethical researcher conduct: A commentary on Ghuge et al. (2026) and Kumar et al. (2026).
articles.authors: Margaret K. Merga, Saiyidi Mat Roni
articles.abstract: This commentary is written for an audience within and beyond academia, as it concerns a dataset from the international community of school library professionals (SLPs). After briefly orienting the reader to commentary and data fabrication, we respond to Ghuge et al. (2026) and Kumar et al. (2026), recent articles with the same corresponding author. Kumar et al. (2026) strongly imply that amongst other researchers, there was a fabrication of data in our 2026 article where some SLP respondents disclosed experiencing significant risk related to their work roles, notably though not exclusively in the US political context. Kumar et al.’s (2026) “reasonable evidence” that we fabricated our data is based on our data availability statement and an opinion poll sent to associates (N=100); this method does not test whether a dataset exists. Ghuge et al. (2026) cites Kumar et al., (2026) to make a similar though far softer claim. We consider Kumar et al. (2026) in relation to ethical conduct in research methods and research respondent risk related to research ecosystem norms. Data sharing cannot be simply conflated with ethical research conduct. If we cannot guarantee anonymity where appropriate, at-risk populations will refuse to participate in social science research.

articles.title: A Productivity Fixated World in the Age of AI: Investigating The Purpose of Human Art
articles.abstract: Modern society increasingly prioritizes final products over the creative process, a trend exacerbated by the rapid adoption of generative AI. This study aims to explore the impact of AI integration into the creative process on subjective well-being and fulfillment, and to determine whether these effects differ between individuals creating for leisure versus those creating for a profession. Within this research, a quantitative-focused survey was conducted with 200 adults, categorized using a 2x2 design: acting as either a hobbyist or a professional illustrator, and either utilizing or not utilizing AI. The data reveals a consistent drop in a person’s well-being across both hobbyist and professional groups when AI is utilized. The differences in fulfillment between hobbyist and professional groups were not statistically significant. While a positive correlation was found between a product-focused mindset and satisfaction among professionals using AI, the overall satisfaction for AI users across the board remained significantly lower than for those who didn’t use AI. These findings suggest that AI integration into creative tasks carries measurable psychological costs by separating the creator from the intrinsically beneficial creative process, along with social costs that taint the creator-audience relationship. These findings underscore the value of human creation, suggesting that the ongoing conversation surrounding AI adoption must extend beyond efficiency to account for value within the human process. An avenue for further research lies within AI use in other fields less traditionally considered a “creative” discipline, such as STEM, which show evidence of having similar psychological benefits arising from the process.

articles.title: Understanding First Nations Disconnection and Reimagining Connection: A yarn between Aboriginal women.
articles.abstract: Connection and belonging are significant processes concerning cultural identity, and for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in Australia, it has been at the forefront of discussions around the Social and Emotional Wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. One area that needs more investigation is that of those individuals on the margins of society who may find access to communities a complex practice. Furthermore, there has been an emergence of recent practices that move connection and belonging beyond more traditional ways of being towards modernity, which includes inclusiveness, accessibility and flexibility for those involved. Drawing on existing literature, collaborative yarning with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and reflective commentary, this article explores the many facets of connection and belonging and the ways in which many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples navigate between cultural traditions, socio-historical challenges and contemporary realities. We call for a reimagining of community spaces and practices to ensure they are inclusive and responsive to the diversity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples’ lived experiences.

articles.title: Do Chatbots Sound Equally Sure in French and in Arabic? A Pilot Audit of Expressed Certainty in ChatGPT and Gemini
articles.abstract: People increasingly ask chatbots about health and public services and pass the answers on to others. Whether they check first may depend on how sure an answer sounds. This pilot audit asks whether the certainty cues that chatbots give change with the language of the question. Ten questions on public health and public services in Morocco were asked once in French and once in Modern Standard Arabic to ChatGPT and Gemini (40 answers). Answers were scored with a bilingual lexicon of hedges and boosters. Both chatbots hedged less in Arabic than in French, and the pattern held under two alternative versions of the lexicon. A model-assisted second coding of 10 answers showed that the lexicon captured boosters well but missed about a third of hedges. With 10 questions and one run each, these results are a first look, not a finding. They motivate a larger audit with repeated runs and human validation.

articles.title: Fairness Perception and Trust Erosion in Competitive Mobile Gaming: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study of a Persian-Language Backgammon Platform
articles.abstract: Fairness perception is a critical yet understudied dimension of player experience in competitive mobile games. This paper presents findings from a five-year longitudinal qualitative study (2022–2026) examining how players construct, reinforce, and communicate beliefs about unfairness in a competitive mobile gaming environment. Using Inductive Thematic Analysis (ITA), we analysed a corpus of more than 52,000 player reviews collected across multiple mobile app marketplaces, supplemented by anonymised customer support interaction transcripts obtained through a research collaboration agreement. Data were collected using a longitudinal sampling design that examined the same calendar month across five consecutive years, enabling the identification of long-term trends while reducing seasonal effects. Analysis identified seven operational themes describing players’ fairness-related beliefs and behaviours, which were subsequently consolidated into three higher-order meta-themes: Perceived Agency (the belief that game systems determine outcomes independently of player skill), Trust Erosion (the progressive reinforcement of manipulation beliefs through negative experiences and platform interactions), and Statistical Misinterpretation (the attribution of probabilistic outcomes to intentional system design). The proportion of 1-star reviews citing fairness-related concerns increased from 3% in 2022 to 18% in 2026, indicating a substantial decline in player trust over the study period. The study further proposes a ten-stage Player Journey of Distrust, mapping the cognitive and emotional progression from initial doubt to entrenched beliefs about manipulation. Findings suggest that fairness complaints are often better understood as expressions of deteriorating trust rather than perceptions of technical malfunction. The paper discusses implications for transparency design, player communication strategies, support systems, and the broader study of trust in digital gaming environments. Keywords: fairness perception; player experience; trust erosion; mobile gaming; thematic analysis; player psychology; app store reviews; cognitive bias; longitudinal qualitative research; trust in digital systems

articles.title: Assaults, Self-Harm, and the Allocation of State Resources in English and Welsh Prisons, 2009-2010 to 2024-2025

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Routine prison allocation in England and Wales is based on staffing, occupancy and regime, but does not incorporate assaults or self-harm. Using 1,727 public-sector establishment-years of Ministry of Justice expenditure and safety data from 2009-2010 to 2024-2025, this article examines whether deteriorating conditions were followed by changes in expenditure. Real expenditure per place fell 28.7 per cent by 2016-2017 before recovering, while prisons retained their relative positions. Higher assault rates were associated with increased expenditure in the following year before 2019-2020, but not thereafter; the interaction test did not establish a change between periods. Self-harm showed no statistically detectable association with subsequent expenditure in either period. Routine allocation continued throughout, but did not consistently respond to deteriorating safety conditions.

articles.title: Reference Observability and Journal Universe Choice in Open Reconstructions of Recursive Journal Metrics
articles.abstract: Open reconstructions of recursive journal indicators can differ from a benchmark along two dimensions: reference observability, which determines which citation records enter the calculation, and the recursive journal universe, over which prestige circulates. We analyze the two dimensions separately in a factorial design. First, we reconstruct Clarivate’s 2024 Article Influence Score (AIS) with OpenAlex data as the Article Network Score (ANS) for a JCR-derived universe (J), the Norwegian Register (N), and the OpenAlex journal universe (A), with ANS defined for 21,706, 22,577, and 107,268 journals, respectively. Then, using a common sample of 15,951 journals, we cross the three universes with two treatments: RAW includes all cited-window articles and reviews, whereas REF retains only those for which OpenAlex records at least one reference. REF improves agreement with AIS in every universe: mean error falls and rank agreement rises. An additional component experiment shows that this improvement does not come from changing the ANS denominator alone, but from its joint change with citation-edge eligibility. Across universes, J and N yield similar results, whereas A has consistently higher errors and lower rank agreement. Robustness checks support the main results on larger journal sets, in the Leiden/CWTS core universe, and in 2023.

articles.title: "They Caught Us Without Any Reason": Waste Pickers' Encounters with Police, Crime and the State in Rawalpindi–Islamabad, Pakistan

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Informal waste pickers (rag-pickers) are routinely portrayed as a source of urban crime, yet little research asks how they themselves experience the police, the state and the illicit economies around them. Drawing on semi-structured interviews in Urdu with 25 waste pickers aged roughly 10 to 50, living in informal settlements (katchi abadis) in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, Pakistan, this article examines their encounters with law-enforcement bodies, their involvement in and victimisation by crime, and their access to government and NGO support. Thematic analysis, informed by street-level bureaucracy and general strain theory, identified four themes: (1) extractive policing, with arbitrary detention, bribes as the price of release, and police ties to employers and dealers; (2) crime as coerced and relational, with drug use and sex work driven by peers, clients, gangs and families; (3) the absent state, with no participant having received government or NGO assistance and BISP applications going unanswered; and (4) constrained pathways into waste picking driven by family need, orphanhood, homelessness and physical incapacity. Most participants said they would leave waste picking if given support. The article calls for protective, non-extractive policing, safeguarding responses to children in sex work and drug use, and outreach that makes social protection reachable. Based on the author's MPhil thesis (National Defence University, Islamabad, 2020). Also archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22981971.

articles.title: All-Male Research Samples Discourage Accurate Science Communication
articles.authors: April Bailey, John Dovidio, Jonas R. Kunst, Marilena Juettemeier, Marianne LaFrance, Gulnaz Anjum, Alexander Scott English, Milan Obaidi, David Lackland Sam, Fatma Yaşın Tekizoğlu
articles.abstract: Research samples have historically overrepresented men, resulting in worse outcomes for women. Even when women are represented, inequity might persist due to underlying differences in how people reason about gender. Theories of androcentrism argue that, in general, people emphasize gender more about women than men. Based on this theory and building on prior archival work, we conducted three preregistered experiments (N = 1,315). Participants read scientific findings based either on all-male or all-female samples. For both, the gender homogeneity of the sample is a key limitation that should be noted when describing results. However, participants were more likely to pick women as a keyword to represent findings based on all-female samples (compared to leaving gender unlisted or listing both women and men) than to pick men to describe identical findings based on all-male samples. Grounded in androcentrism theory, this work has practical implications for accurate science communication and gender equity.

articles.title: Research and Impact of Prompt Engineering Nexus on Programming and Routine Tasks: Exploring Future Possible Directions

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Prompt engineering has developed as a transformative subfield in artificial intelligence (AI), enabling humans to enhance AI systems through structured (PROLOG-like) instructions to perform specific tasks. This paper shines a light on its multi-dimensional impact on programming, routine tasks and broader AI applications, drawing on insights from recent studies. By using techniques such as parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), zero-shot learning, multi-shot learning and linguistic feature analysis, prompt engineering often is used to tackle remaining issues in software engineering (SE), language processing (NLP) and AI safety. The body of literature highlights its role in optimizing AI performance, reducing computational overhead and reducing biases. Additionally, it highlights critical gaps in current methodologies, such as the comparative energy intensity of state-of-art large language models (LLMs) and the requirements for adaptive and scalable prompt crafting strategies. Finally, the paper suggests future directions for research, highlighting the importance of human-centered design and collaboration to advance the field.

articles.title: Unexpected heat suppresses emigration from the world's poorest countries
articles.abstract: Whether climate stress displaces people or traps them in place is unresolved. The common intuition is displacement: crops fail, heat becomes unliveable and people leave. Other work predicts the opposite for poor countries, where migration abroad is expensive and the shock that sharpens the wish to leave can destroy the means to go. Estimates disagree, partly because realized temperature mixes warming that households anticipated with warming they did not. I isolate the unanticipated part with temperature forecast errors, the warmth or cold a forecast missed, and estimate their effect on monthly international migration from countries holding most of the world’s population. Here I show that unexpected warmth does not detectably move migration on average, but that in low-income countries an unexpectedly hot month lowers departures over the following year. No richer income group shows a detectable response. The migration suppression is strongest where incomes depend on agriculture, also appears outside the growing season and leaves in-migration flat, consistent with heat removing the means to move. For the poorest countries, unexpected heat may hold people back rather than push them abroad. Projections and policies built around displacement may overstate departures from these countries and overlook those who cannot afford to leave.

articles.title: Larger, younger, faster, harder: expansion, transformation, and inequality in YouTube’s creator economy (2019–2026)
articles.authors: Bernhard Rieder, Adrian Padilla, Ariadna Matamoros-Fernández, Òscar Coromina
articles.abstract: The growth of YouTube's creator economy raises a question that accounts of individual success and precarity cannot settle: how are the conditions of participation changing across the platform? Comparing two population-scale crawls from 2019 and 2026, we examine expansion, changes in production, and the distribution of attention across millions of channels. The population above the 1,000-subscriber threshold for advertising monetization grew from 4.4 million to 24.5 million, while its video catalogues grew ninefold. Expansion was strongest in South, Southeast, and East Asia, with India's share of channels declaring a country rising from 10 to 27 percent. This growth accompanied substantial turnover: most channels recorded in 2019 had no recent upload in 2026, and continued participation differed sharply by prior standing. Production also changed fundamentally. Median video duration fell from 247 to 60 seconds, with shortening across every content category and channel size. Among channels above 100,000 subscribers, new entrants accounted for most of the shift toward short form, while most continuing incumbents also shortened their output. Attention became more concentrated even among the same channels observed at both dates, and advertising revenue grew more slowly than the population meeting the subscriber threshold. These findings show how the output imperative extends from producing more to adapting what is produced, while sustained participation remains sharply unequal. They also place the increasingly Asian geography of the creator economy at the center of questions about platform labor, opportunity, and precarity.

articles.title: Beyond the Joke: A Thematic Content Analysis of Russian-Linked Meme Pages Targeting Azerbaijan
articles.abstract: As internet memes evolved from mere entertainment into a tool of digital propaganda, their role in modern warfare has become increasingly significant. This study examines their role in the case of Russian-linked information operations targeting the Azerbaijani audience on Facebook. While the existing literature on meme-based Russian propaganda focuses heavily on the United States and Ukraine, the South Caucasus, one of the important regions of Russia’s “near abroad” policy, remains overlooked. The research addresses this critical gap by analyzing how these strategies are adapted to Azerbaijan's specific cultural and political context. The study relies on qualitative, multimodal analysis and emergent coding of 78 memes from nine Russian-linked Facebook pages targeting Azerbaijan between January 2023 and December 2024. The analysis identifies four consistent themes (the negative othering of the West, the discrediting of Western leaders, the reframing of the Nagorno-Karabakh Conflict, and the promotion of Azerbaijani sovereignty) and various propaganda techniques that have already been revealed in existing studies.
