The research paper concludes that these pages conduct a systematic influence campaign that sophisticatedly blends pro-Russian narratives with culturally conservative and patriotic domestic sentiments to resonate with the local audience.

articles.title: Did local authorities lose revenue following banning unhealthy food advertising?

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: UK local authorities are increasingly exploring restrictions for the advertising of unhealthy foods on their estates to promote healthier food environments. Concerns about effects on revenue can be a barrier to progress. In this study, we provide preliminary evidence that these policies did not negatively affect total advertising revenue across four local authorities in North West England. In some cases, we found that revenue increased post-implementation.

articles.title: Product Market Reform and Enterprise Software Diffusion: Evidence from European Industries
articles.abstract: This paper examines whether product-market reforms in upstream network sectors are associated with faster diffusion of enterprise software in downstream European industries. The analysis combines Eurostat data on Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) adoption with OECD ETCR and REGIMPACT indicators for 24 economies and 13 industries over 2010–2021. Reform exposure is constructed using major annual regulatory declines and fixed 2010 US input-output weights, while the empirical specification includes country-by-interval, industry-by-interval and country-industry fixed effects. Industries more exposed to major reforms experience faster growth in the combined ERP-CRM adoption index. At the median nonzero reform exposure, the estimate corresponds to approximately 1.5 percentage points of additional adoption growth. The response is stronger for CRM, while ERP is smaller and less precisely estimated. Minor and moderate regulatory changes show no comparable relationship. The results remain similar across alternative samples, reform thresholds and controls for the initial stage of software diffusion. The findings connect upstream product-market reform to downstream diffusion of organizational technologies.

articles.title: Conceptualizing Political Consumerism in the Attention Economy
articles.authors: Christopher Starke, Claes de Vreese, Natali Helberger
articles.abstract: Social media platforms increasingly become targets of politically and ethically motivated user protest, yet existing approaches do not sufficiently explain how deliberate platform use can operate as political participation. This conceptual paper extends the established concept of political consumerism to the attention economy, defining it as individuals’ market-oriented behaviors to punish or reward social media platforms on political or ethical grounds. It argues that three main factors constrain political consumerism on social media platforms: opaque value extraction, limited ethical alternatives, and high switching costs. Because political consumerism can take many forms, the paper suggests distinguishing user actions by their economic impact and whether they signal user preferences to the platform company. It further explains how social media literacy and regulation can improve the legibility and actionability of these practices. Finally, it outlines methodological implications for studying political consumerism through mixed-method designs that combine user motivations with behavioral data.

articles.title: Resilience in a Discordant Security Culture: Georgia between Institutional Continuity and Political Realignment
articles.abstract: Challenging the common understanding in the relevant literature, this study reconceptualizes resilience to hybrid threats as a politically mediated process rather than purely a matter of institutional capacity-building. To examine how policy frameworks and political rhetoric interact to shape resilience, it traces Georgia’s security culture in the aftermath of the Russo-Georgian war. Through intertextual discourse analysis, the article cross-examines the institutional architecture of digital resilience, encompassing cybersecurity (systemic), media regulation (protective) and media literacy (empowerment) measures, with the government’s shifting rhetoric (2023–2025), while interview data provide contextual insights. The analysis reveals a discordant security culture manifested in fragmented governance and discursive struggle over resilience. Although formal policy frameworks normatively align with the West and consistently identify Russia as the principal security threat, governmental rhetoric portrays the same Western actors as sources of foreign interference and prioritizes political autonomy over cooperation while still invoking commitments to the constitutionally enshrined Euro-Atlantic trajectory. This dichotomy between institutional design and political discourse results in strategic ambiguity. It suggests that in hybrid regimes formal frameworks may function symbolically to signal external alignment, while practice is determined by short-term political calculations and discretionary authority, leaving institutions and societies vulnerable to evolving forms of foreign interference.

articles.title: From Desktop to Spatial Interfaces: UX Design Implications of Evolving Interaction Paradigms
articles.abstract: This study examines how the transition from screen-based interaction paradigms to spatial interfaces affects established user experience principles and design considerations. The study is guided by the following research question: How does the transition from screen-based interaction paradigms to spatial interfaces affect established UX principles and design considerations? Apple Vision Pro and visionOS are examined as one case. The corpus consists of 60 selected Human Interface Guidelines pages, 76 WWDC sessions, the Apple Vision Pro User Guide, and notes from researcher observation. The HIG and WWDC materials were analyzed qualitatively and coded using four dimensions: consistency, feedback, affordance, and information architecture. The analysis suggests that established UX principles remain relevant in spatial interfaces, although the way they are implemented changes. This study describes that change through three categories: retention, adaptation, and extension. Some familiar purposes and structures remain in place, others are adapted through spatial interaction, and some design concerns expand to include the user’s body and surrounding environment. Familiar structures such as windows, controls, and navigation remain important, but visionOS adds gaze, gesture, depth, distance, sound, anchoring, and immersion as additional design mechanisms. From this pattern, the study proposes selective spatiality: spatial presentation, immersion, and embodied interaction are most useful when they support the task, not simply because they are available on the platform. In the Vision Pro case, effective spatial UX comes from keeping familiar interaction structures while adding spatial features only where they are useful. Designers must also consider comfort, attention, accessibility, environmental awareness, and hardware limits. Because the study examines one platform and does not include independent user testing, its findings should be interpreted within that scope.

articles.title: Behavioural Sociology of Humans and Machines
articles.authors: Taha Yasseri, Hao Cui, Nico Mutzner
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly participates in communication, decision-making, and collective action, making the social organisation of human–machine interaction central to Hybrid Intelligence (HI). This chapter reviews the behavioural sociology of humans and machines through an HI lens, examining how interaction and feedback shape the combination of human and artificial capabilities. Drawing on sociology, social psychology, human–computer interaction, organisational studies, collective intelligence, and science and technology studies, it traces processes from individual social perception to cooperation in hybrid groups and organisational and institutional arrangements. Particular attention is given to how machine participation alters familiar mechanisms: social categorisation attaches expectations to designed identities, reciprocity may involve unequal social obligations, and algorithmic recommendations acquire authority through organisational practices. The chapter distinguishes observable machine behaviour from human interpretations of intention, understanding, and moral responsibility. It also considers how behavioural effects can extend beyond direct human–machine encounters, while separating established findings from proposed longer-term consequences. It argues that the benefits of HI depend on how roles, incentives, reliance, and accountability are organised, and identifies priorities for empirical research on these evolving sociotechnical arrangements.

articles.title: From Water Scarcity to Paceklik: Ecological Memory in Banyumas Literary and Expressive Traditions
articles.abstract: Abstract Water is more than a physical necessity in communities whose everyday life has historically been closely connected with agriculture, seasonal rainfall, and the availability of water. It can become an object of desire, ritual expectation, narrative valuation, social celebration, and material anxiety. This article examines how such relationships are articulated across four Banyumasan literary and expressive traditions: Banyu Emas, Cowongan, Ricik-Ricik, and Ahmad Tohari’s Ronggeng Dukuh Paruk. The study employs qualitative comparative interpretation within an ecocritical framework and uses the concept of ecological memory in a deliberately bounded cultural sense. Rather than treating ecological memory as proof of a population’s psychological recollection of particular environmental events, the article defines it as the recurrent cultural articulation of human–environment relationships through forms in which environmental experience can be represented, performed, retained, and reinterpreted. The analysis finds that the four corpus units do not constitute a single environmental narrative or a continuous chain of cultural transmission. Their significance lies instead in the different ways cultural form transforms environmental experience. Banyu Emas renders water scarcity as a condition that gives water extraordinary value; Cowongan turns uncertainty over rainfall into ritual supplication and collective anticipation; Ricik-Ricik constructs the arrival of drizzle or rain as an occasion of happiness, humor, sociability, and play; while Ronggeng Dukuh Paruk connects drought with agricultural disruption, paceklik, food scarcity, and bodily vulnerability. The comparison extends ecological-memory discussion by demonstrating that environmental memory can encompass positive affect as well as crisis, including happiness, relief, humor, and anticipation. It also suggests that recurrence should not be confused with transmission and that continuity may occur through transformation rather than preservation. Ecological memory, in this formulation, persists because environmental relationships remain culturally productive even when the forms and meanings through which they are expressed change.

articles.title: Enduring and Emerging Issues in Early Childhood Home Visiting: A Survey of Key Interest Groups
articles.authors: Allison West, Lauren Klein, Kimberly Mihayo, Kay O'Neill, Jane Daniels, Jon Korfmacher
articles.abstract: Background: Early childhood home visiting is a voluntary, two generation approach to promote the health and well-being of pregnant women and families with young children. The purpose of this survey was to assess enduring and emerging issues in home visiting within an evolving service delivery landscape. Methods: We recruited participants from a broad range of home visiting interest groups through an established practice-based research network. Participants completed a survey in which they selected the issues that were most concerning to them from a predetermined list and provided reasons for their selections as open text responses. We calculated the frequency with which each issue was endorsed and synthesized qualitative explanations for the top third of all issues selected. Results: The issues endorsed most frequently were supporting families when community resources aren’t available, funding stability, family recruitment and engagement, workforce well-being and retention, and administrative burden. Conclusions: Survey results highlight the strong influence of community context and funding on home visiting implementation and outcomes, enduring questions regarding family recruitment and engagement, and opportunities to support and strengthen the workforce. Findings will inform collaborative, applied research to identify gaps, develop solutions, and advance home visiting policy and practice.

articles.title: How does the level of media propaganda literacy differ among individuals under 18, between 18 and 30, and over 30 in Uzbekistan, and how does this difference impact their vulnerability to misinformation and critical thinking skills?
articles.abstract: This research investigates how varying levels of media propaganda literacy across different age groups in Uzbekistan impact susceptibility to misinformation and critical thinking. By categorizing participants into three distinct age groups—those under 18, between 18 and 30, and over 30—the study identifies generational differences shaped by historical and technological contexts. Data collected through surveys and interviews reveal that while younger generations rely more on social media and demonstrate greater adaptability to digital information, older individuals remain dependent on traditional media like television, often lacking critical fact-checking skills. Despite a high level of self-reported understanding of concepts like "propaganda," significant knowledge gaps persist, particularly among older participants, highlighting the enduring impact of Soviet-era media practices. The findings underscore the need for targeted media literacy initiatives tailored to age-specific vulnerabilities to bridge generational divides and empower all citizens to evaluate information critically

articles.title: An Integrated Multi-Method Approach to Television Studies in the Streaming Era: the Production, Representation, and Reception of Gender Violence on Norwegian Screens
articles.abstract: By merging textual analysis with production interviews and audience studies, this article aims to develop a multi-method approach to television texts. The method proves particularly useful to investigate audiences’ interpretation of gender violence on screen and how this is integrated within a Public Service Broadcaster’s societal mission and national audiences’ perception of the broadcaster. The article focuses on the most popular Norwegian TV series to date Exit (2019-2023) distributed by the national NRK, as a product of enlightening entertainment. It questions how aesthetic choices create realism and how different audiences relate to the reality presented as authentic and relatable. It also interrogates how audiences’ perception of the national broadcaster affect their interpretation of the series.

articles.title: Pretender: When Organizations Perform Competence Instead of Creating Value
articles.abstract: This paper develops the concept of Pretender to explain a condition in which organizations increasingly prioritize demonstrating that they function properly over producing the substantive value those functions are meant to create. The idea originated from an everyday Japanese expression, gokko (ごっこ), loosely meaning “playing at” a role or activity. Here, gokko does not imply deliberate deception, incompetence, or conscious fakery. Rather, it points to situations in which management, expertise, reflection, adjudication, or organizational response becomes partially detached from its substantive function while retaining value as evidence that the function exists. To conceptualize this process, the paper distinguishes among Substantive Function, Competence Performance, and Evidence of Function, and defines Pretender Drift as the gradual shift by which Evidence of Function becomes more organizationally salient than Substantive Function. The framework is positioned in relation to goal displacement, ceremonial conformity and decoupling, means–ends decoupling, organized hypocrisy, impression management, organizational legitimacy, and the audit society. Its distinctive focus is not merely that means and ends become separated, but that practices may continue and even expand because they serve as evidence of competence, professionalism, control, fairness, or appropriate organizational response. The paper examines several levels of Pretender: Strong-Person Pretender, Managerial Pretender, Professional Pretender, Procedural Pretender, and Organizational Pretender. It further develops the Pretender Management Loop, in which expanded control creates new opportunities for observable deviation, which in turn justifies further control, and the Nested Pretender Structure, in which role-level, procedural, and organizational performances mutually reinforce one another. Finally, it considers how Voice, Silence, Adaptation, and Exit may shape the long-term reproduction of Pretender Culture through organizational selection. The argument is not against rules, formal procedures, professional standards, audits, training, or discipline. The central question is whether these forms remain connected to the outcomes they were created to produce. Pretender begins when proving that work was done becomes more important than asking what the work actually made better.

articles.title: The Four Ways of Knowing: Revising the 4P Model of Knowing Through a Non-dual and Reflexive Perspective
articles.authors: Hüseyin Beyköylü, John Vervaeke, Daniel Meling
articles.abstract: The discipline of epistemology seeks to delineate the diverse forms of knowledge that inform our lives, from the concrete, embodied experiences that shape our everyday perceptions to the abstract, theoretical constructs that drive scientific inquiry. Cognitive science uniquely extends this project by exploring the human and non-human minds that afford knowing and understanding. Building on this legacy, Vervaeke and Mastropietro's 4P model of knowing integrates four interrelated ways of knowing: propositional, procedural, perspectival, and participatory, into a unified, non-representational, and process-oriented framework. In this paper, we first provide an integrated overview of what we term the classical 4P model by exploring the ways of knowing constituting it, introducing the relationship of asymmetric dependence between the four ways of knowing, and situating the model within the pragmatic concerns that motivated its development. We then offer a critique of this model informed by enactive cognitive science and insights from the Madhyamaka and Yogācāra traditions of Buddhist epistemology. Finally, we revise the classical 4P model by clarifying and refining the relationships among the four ways of knowing through a non-dual and reflexive treatment, and discuss how this revised framework can inform fields as diverse as education, psychotherapy, and religious and contemplative pedagogy, demonstrating its potential for addressing contemporary challenges.

articles.title: Partial Exit and Bargaining Power: How Exit Menus Shape Institutional Design
articles.abstract: A government can often refuse a collective undertaking in more than one way. It may leave the organization, stay out of one initiative, withhold a contribution or block one legal route. I extend exit, voice and loyalty to such exit menus. The refusal a government would actually choose fixes both its own fallback and the others' cost of disagreement. A narrower exit can therefore activate leverage or displace a threat that had secured accommodation. Others who still want the government inside can pay it, restrict common uses or change the scale of provision, and relative marginal costs shape which margin adjusts. Accommodation need not benefit its recipient. When what refusal yields depends on the capacity on offer, an improved alternative can lead the others to build less and leave a retained government worse off despite larger payments. Euro-area rescue finance documents decision-specific refusal rules, rejected protections and reciprocal conditions.

articles.title: Similar disruptions, different reactions? Refugee crises and the politicization of immigration in Sweden and Switzerland
articles.authors: Marco Bitschnau, Didier Ruedin, Anders Hellström, Marie Sundström
articles.abstract: We investigate how major refugee crises affected the immigration debate in Sweden and Switzerland, two countries that have long been among the most popular European destinations for immigrants in general and refugees in particular. Analysing claims from newspapers during two crises, the Balkans refugee crisis of the 1990s and the European refugee crisis of 2015–16 (N=3,593), we find (1) fairly diverse patterns of politicization, with slightly greater polarization in Switzerland but higher salience peaks in Sweden; (2) no significant differences in how actors position themselves in relation to the status quo; and (3) substantial differences in how they use certain frames. We conclude that despite their proximity to immigration matters, refugee crises do not always lead to more politicized debates. There may be some crisis impact—but certainly no reason for crisis determinism. Instead, factors such as the domestic context and the relative shock value of each crisis appear to be relevant and should be given more consideration.

articles.title: What QCA Cannot See: Identification Bounds for Configurational Solutions with Missing Set Memberships
articles.abstract: Qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) needs a membership score for every case in every set, and applied studies commonly remove cases whose scores are missing. In a truth table, removal can turn a configuration that exists but was not scored into a logical remainder available as a simplifying assumption. We propose partial-identification QCA (PI-QCA). Each missing score is represented by an interval, every completion is considered, and the analysis reports exact bounds for the consistency and coverage of any term, the sure solution (the terms present in the solution of every completion), the possible region, bracketed by an inner bound from sampled completions and an outer bound from enumeration, and the identification gap. A solution outside the outer bound is produced by no completion. By construction, the sure solution cannot contain a term absent from the complete-data solution. In 900 simulated data sets its sampled approximation also satisfied this in every replicate, whereas case deletion and mean imputation returned false terms about as often as the complete-data analysis on average but up to 22 percentage points more often under some missingness mechanisms. The price is an empty sure solution in 71–95% of replicates when a fifth of the scores were missing. In an illustration with 131 economies, deletion returns a solution that no completion produces when the outcome is kept at its recorded values. Reanalyses of two published studies find a certified empty sure solution for one outcome and, for another, published solutions attained by none of 208 sampled completions.

articles.title: Group Affect and the Electoral Protection of Transgender Rights
articles.abstract: When does positive affect for a minority group translate into electoral protection for its rights? We examine this question for trans rights, which are being rolled back in many democracies. We ran a pre-registered experiment with 1,500 British adults in May 2025, weeks after the UK Supreme Court restricted the legal definition of `woman' to biological sex. Respondents chose between candidates from their preferred party who either endorsed or opposed the Supreme Court ruling, alongside other traits. We find a preference for candidates who endorse trans rights retrenchment that transcends much of the left-right divide. Crucially, although warm feelings toward trans people are twice as common as cold ones, cold affect translates more readily and more strongly into candidate choice. This asymmetry produces an overall electoral advantage for candidates endorsing trans rights retrenchment, with only those holding the warmest feelings toward trans people preferring candidates who oppose the ruling.

articles.title: Demographer Views about U.S. Fertility: Results from a Survey
articles.abstract: The view that birth rates in the U.S. (where the total fertility rate is now 1.57) is a crisis – even an existential crisis – is increasingly common, but academic demography has not adopted this frame. Demographers should not expect unquestioning acceptance of our views on population issues, but it is useful to make our perspective known, individually as well as collectively. To that end, I report on a new survey of 190 self-identified U.S. demographic researchers (either U.S. nationals or based in the U.S.) on birth rates and population trends. The sample was drawn from demography journal authors, with a response rate of 27.7%. Results show that only 3% agreed the U.S. is in a “demographic crisis.” A majority agreed that government should take measures in order to increase fertility if the total fertility rate were to fall to 0.8 – while 43% believe governments should “never intervene” to raise birth rates. On the other hand, with “the right policies,” 84% agreed the U.S. would benefit from substantially increased immigration. Asked to rank global population issues for the coming years, respondents ranked climate change, aging, and inequality most important, with low birth rates rating eighth out of 12 issues.

articles.title: Solidarity at War: The Quest for the Decolonial Subject in Russian Feminism
articles.abstract: Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine a new debate in transnational feminism and feminist security studies has framed decolonisation as a precondition for solidarity. This discussion has primarily focused on relations between Western and Ukrainian and Central and Eastern European feminists, leaving Russian feminism largely unexamined. This article thus asks whether and to what extent these decolonial debates have travelled to Russia by analysing the Feminist Anti-War Resistance (FAR). Drawing on a content analysis of FAR’s Telegram channel and its self-published newspaper the article shows that while FAR has an awareness of decolonial critiques, the engagement remains limited in breadth and direction. References to decolonisation and imperialism are marginal, concentrated in the early months of the full-scale invasion, and inwardlooking, focusing on internal hierarchies within the Russian Federation while eclipsing Ukraine. The article concludes with an assessment of the implications for future crossborder solidarity between Russian and Ukrainian feminists.

articles.title: A Representation-Theoretic Method for Analyzing Order Dependence in Decomposition Analysis: An Application to Fertility Change in Korea
articles.abstract: Decomposition analysis is widely used to attribute changes in an aggregate outcome to changes in its underlying components. When several factors change simultaneously, however, sequential replacement generally yields different contributions depending on the order in which factors are replaced. The Shapley value resolves this problem by averaging marginal contributions over all possible orders, but the variation across those orders is itself potentially informative. This study proposes a decomposition method that analyzes this order dependence rather than averaging it away. For each factor, its contribution over all decomposition paths is treated as a function on the symmetric group. Harsanyi dividends are used to express path dependence in terms of interaction components, and irreducible representations of the symmetric group are then used to decompose the variance of path-specific contributions into interpretable spectral components. This framework distinguishes three properties of a decomposition result: average contribution, order instability, and the interaction complexity underlying that instability. For a decomposition with six factors, the method generates 64 counterfactual states and 720 replacement paths. Synthetic experiments confirm the predicted relationship between interaction order and admissible representation components and verify the numerical decomposition of order variance to machine precision. The empirical application examines fertility change among Korean women aged 20–49 using population size, age structure, marital composition, parity composition among married women, nonmarital fertility, and parity-specific marital fertility. Between 2000 and 2024, marital composition and parity-specific marital fertility contributed strongly to the decline in births, while changes in parity composition substantially offset that decline. The results also show that path-specific contributions can vary substantially around their Shapley means: for marital composition, parity composition and parity-specific marital fertility, the path standard deviation amounts to roughly 31–42% of the total change between 2000 and 2024. Cross-period differences in spectral structure, however, are strongly shaped by the magnitude of change over each interval. The proposed method extends decomposition analysis from the allocation of average contributions to the analysis of the full distribution and structure of path-specific contributions. It therefore provides an additional diagnostic layer for studying interaction, robustness, and structural dependence in multi-factor decomposition.

articles.title: Building better parenting leave survey data: A repository of survey questions for comparative policy analysis
articles.authors: Cassandra Engeman, Marie Valentova, Laurène Thil, Anna Stastna, Anne Hartung, Alzbeta Bartova, Ivana Dobrotic, Ásdís A. Arnalds, Stephan Köppe, Elitsa Dimitrova

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: This document presents a repository of questions that can be used in cross-national comparative surveys to collect data on parenting leave. With our collated and proposed questions, we aim to assist researchers and data collection agencies build better parenting leave data to understand when and how parents use such provisions. In the following sections, we present questions related to measuring (1) formal and perceived eligibility for leave provisions, (2) leave use and non-use, (3) reasons for non-use, and (4) views about parenting leave. While questions in the first three sections primarily measure behaviour, we include questions about parents’ views, because they can inform behaviour. Each of these four main sections includes our research- and theory-based motivations for the phrasing, inclusion and design of the questions as well as their shortcomings.

articles.title: My (22m) Girlfriend (23f) Comes Home and Does Nothing”– Gendered Perceptions of Paid and Unpaid Work in Reddit Relationship Discussions over Time
articles.authors: Birgit Zeyer-Gliozzo, Johanna Hölzl, Gundula Zoch, Philipp Doebler
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic reignited longstanding debates around gender inequalities in paid and unpaid work. While survey research has advanced our understanding of these disparities, it typically relies on predefined categories and is susceptible to social desirability and recall bias. Online postings, by contrast, capture intimate experiences in real time but rarely include demographic attributes. We leverage a unique dataset of discussions in Reddit relationship communities that combines rich descriptions of conflicts around (un)paid work with demographic information to examine: Which topics do men and women discuss in relationship conflicts around paid and unpaid work? We use Large Language Models (LLMs) and systematically vary GPT-family models and prompting strategies to classify manifest (demographic information) and latent variables (whether posts discuss romantic relationships, paid, and unpaid work) in Reddit posts. Using classifications from the best-performing approach, we apply Structural Topic Models to explore which topics partners discuss and how discussions evolve over time. We find temporary pandemic shifts in topics, and women more often discuss mental health in paid work-related conflicts, while men more frequently emphasize career objectives. In conflicts related to unpaid work, men more frequently express concerns about sexual intimacy. Our analysis offers new insights into topics driving relationship conflicts around (un)paid work. We also contribute to the growing literature on LLMs’ capabilities and limitations in classifying social-science constructs. By combining demographic information with sensitive narratives, our dataset captures forms of relational conflict rarely accessible in survey or social-media research, opening promising avenues for future research.

articles.title: Ecological responsibility, wellbeing, and transformative reach: a three-dimensional framework for assessing ecovillages as social innovations toward sustainability
articles.abstract: Ecovillages are collective experiments in maintaining wellbeing within planetary limits, testing whether human flourishing can be maintained while material throughput is reduced. Drawing on a critical narrative review of intentional communities, ecological economics, commons governance, and self-determination theory, we propose a three- dimension, two-layer framework joining ecological limits, wellbeing, and the propagation dynamics of social innovations. The outcome layer includes five elements across three dimensions: critical natural capital and biophysical flows (ecological), material sufficiency and eudaimonic wellbeing (wellbeing), and transformative effect (transformative), an outward axis specific to social innovations. The lever layer includes three transversal levers: a sufficiency economy that drives throughput reduction, a commons governance built on Ostrom's design principles, and a propagation infrastructure that carries practices beyond the host site. Empirically, ecovillages deliver 35 to 80% footprint reductions and achieve partial closure of nutrient cycles. They meet a decent material floor through commons-based provisioning while sustaining or improving wellbeing. They propagate practices via transmission, replication, partnerships, and political influence. Four structural challenges constrain systemic contribution: limited actual impact on ecological, host- territory, and cultural dimensions; dependence on the mainstream provisioning system; barriers to scale (demanding resident profiles, high attrition); and social selection. We argue that ecovillages are best understood as generative laboratories of transposable knowledge and living alternatives that act as vectors of cultural changes. We propose an agenda for a wider community-based transition, associating multi-scale architectures with supportive economic models, facilitative institutions, and a deliberate research program. We situate this Northern articulation within a wider pluriverse of place-based sustainability projects, of which ecovillages are one strand among many.

articles.title: Given and Chosen Ties: Status, Personal Networks, and Political Behaviour in Britain
articles.abstract: Political participation in Britain is stratified not only by where people stand but by who stands with them. Bringing social network analysis to the study of social stratification, this article draws on ego-networks from the British Household Panel Survey, which link respondents to their closest friends and to partners and relatives who are themselves panel members. It examines how the status of these networks relates to turnout, political interest, and party choice across four general elections, and whether given ties, such as parents and siblings, differ from chosen ties, such as partners and friends. Status homophily is strongest among friends. The status of partners, friends, and the family of origin is associated with each outcome. The family of origin is as closely associated as chosen ties, and more closely with interest, whereas adult children stand largely apart. Status also reaches further than behaviour: two steps from ego, alters' status is still associated with ego's turnout, while their turnout is not. These associations reflect stable differences between people, pointing to durable status milieux. Between 1992 and 2005, these milieux came to separate voters from abstainers more, and Labour from Conservative voters less.

articles.title: The Evolutionary Hearth: An Environment-Dependent Game-Theoretic Framework for Javanese Maternal Domestic Pedagogy
articles.abstract: This study introduces the Principle of Conditional Cultural Adaptiveness, establishing that the evolutionary performance of cultural strategies depends strictly on environmental state variables and shifts through equilibrium migration as those macro-conditions change. Modernity is formally conceptualized not as cultural erosion, but as equilibrium migration between state-dependent optima. Existing scholarly interpretations of Javanese maternal domesticity and the construct of kanca wingking frequently emphasize patriarchal gender hierarchies, symbolic cosmology, or moral norms without formally modeling how domestic practices dynamically adjust to resource volatility, environmental hazards, and shifting household bargaining power. We develop an environment-dependent game-theoretic frame work linking selected maternal instructions to material resource allocation, homeostatic regulation, risk management, health capital investment, cultural information transmission, and costly signaling. By integrating ethnographic philology with evolutionary game theory, bargaining theory, dynamic optimization, and eco-evolutionary feedback modeling, this research provides a formal computational social science framework for representing cultural persistence and transformation while explicitly differentiating stable household equilibria from equitable distributions of welfare.

articles.title: In Silico Advertising Tests
articles.authors: Marta Trales, Guillaume Hochard, Christophe Benavent
articles.abstract: This research examines whether large language model agents can produce analytically useful evidence for advertising testing when treated as synthetic respondents rather than as substitutes for human consumers. We report an in-silico comparative post-test of two television advertisements in the French telecommunications market, conducted on a panel of 800 profile-conditioned consumer agents. The study evaluates the synthetic corpus through internal validity criteria: whether the questionnaire covers the main dimensions of advertising response, whether evaluative dimensions form coherent relations, whether the two stimuli are discriminated across preference labels, scores, lexical patterns and semantic embeddings, and whether responses vary intelligibly across social profiles. The results indicate that the synthetic panel produces structured and interpretable evidence. The contribution is not that the analysis discovers a contrast invisible in the advertisements themselves: Bouygues and Orange are clearly built around different persuasive registers. Rather, the contribution is methodological. The synthetic-interview pipeline consistently recovers and differentiates these registers across preference labels, scores, lexical patterns and semantic comparisons. Bouygues is associated mainly with creative, humorous and memorable qualities, while Orange is associated with reliability, informativeness, purchase orientation and overall preference. This structure is visible quantitatively in the main six dimensional coding scheme. Among all 800 synthetic agents, Bouygues leads on creativity (83.6% versus 14.8% for Orange), whereas Orange leads on informationseeking or consideration (76.8% versus 14.8% for Bouygues) and overall preference (54.8% versus 20.6% for Bouygues), with the remaining responses classified as mixed or neutral. The analysis remains deliberately limited to synthetic respondents. Claims about similarity to human preferences or market behaviour would require external comparison with representative human data or market-level indicators.

articles.title: Polity Size and Women's Representation: Evidence from Two Large-scale Boundary Reforms
articles.authors: Moa Frödin-Gruneau, Jan Teorell, Kåre Vernby
articles.abstract: Do larger polities hinder gender parity in elected office? We theorize that when populations grow faster than elected assemblies, a “seat congestion” effect intensifies competition for nominations, enabling men candidates to crowd out women. We test this argument using two nationwide natural experiments: Swedish municipal amalgamations in 1952 and 1973 that abruptly increased electorates. We track the effects in newly digitized historical panel data. Where electorate-per-seat ratios rose, growth in women's representation slowed. Decomposition analyses show that expanding councils only partially offsets congestion. By identifying polity size as a systematic brake on descriptive representation, the study adds a demographic dimension to debates on institutional design and points to an overlooked cost of increasing jurisdictional size.

articles.title: Organicity And Structural Coincidence. Intellectual Activity Across Fields
articles.abstract: Intellectual activity is examined as a crucial component in the formation of dominant principles of perception, classification, and action. Drawing on Bourdieu’s field theory, the analysis focuses on the structural coincidence of struggles across relatively autonomous fields, showing how concordant principles may emerge without central coordination and contribute to naturalising the established order. Gramsci’s concepts of organicity, intellectual function, civil society, and common sense broaden this perspective by extending the range of agents, practices, and institutions implicated in hegemonic processes. This also foregrounds their relational and pedagogical dimensions and the need for an empirical inventory of the sites and symbolic forms through which common sense takes shape. Hegemony is thus treated as the contingent outcome of differentiated struggles whose effects become aligned across fields. A case study of agricultural capitalism in Romania illustrates the empirical operationalisation of this framework. For a fuller discussion and further developments of these themes: https://www.routledge.com/On-Gramsci-and-Bourdieu-Hegemony-Fields-and-Tools-for-Social-Research/Puoti-Roger/p/book/9781041299523

articles.title: Why We Cling to Flawed Influencers: Psychological Mechanisms Behind Loyalty to Deceptive Social Media Figures
articles.abstract: Abstract Existing studies on loyalty to social media influencers have mainly focused on cognitive dissonance, parasocial bonding, halo effect, social identity, and just world belief, each in isolation. This paper advances another argument: that these five mechanisms occur not independently but in a predictable sequence, each reducing psychological resistance to the next, producing loyalties more resistant than any single mechanism alone. We call this the compounding loyalty model. Cognitive dissonance is the initial motivation causing a follower to realise something is wrong; parasocial bonding makes rationalisation a requirement, not an option; the halo effect provides a surface level base for maintaining trust despite misbehaviours; social identity makes loyalty costly to lose; and just world belief provides a final, motivated argument that deception did not happen at all. We draw this model from cases including James Charles (2021) and Ramon Abbas, convicted of fraud in 2022. Media literacy, ethical marketing and platform policy are discussed. Keywords: Influencers, social media, Cognitive dissonance, Para-social relationships, Halo effect, social identity theory, just world hypothesis, Compounding loyalty model.

articles.title: Research on Han Nationalism in China in the 2020s (VIII): Five Ideological Tendencies within Han Nationalism and Their Real-World Demands
articles.abstract: This article is an exploratory study in the series “Research on Han Nationalism in China in the 2020s.” It examines different ideological tendencies within Han nationalist discourse on the Chinese Internet. Unlike approaches that treat Han nationalism as a single political position, this article argues that contemporary Han nationalism on the Chinese Internet is not a unified movement with a common political program, but a collection of ideological tendencies formed around different real-world problems. Based on long-term observation of relevant online discourse, historical narratives, cultural phenomena, and public discussions, the article identifies five ideal types: establishment Han nationalism, renunciation-oriented Han nationalism, left-wing Han nationalism, cultural Han nationalism, and right-wing Han nationalism. These five tendencies primarily focus, respectively, on policy correction; central–local relations and fiscal responsibility; ethnic and class inequality; Han cultural identity; and population decline and the long-term demographic continuity of the Han. Although they share dissatisfaction with some differentiated ethnic policies and particular historical narratives, they differ substantially in their explanations of the causes of these problems and in their proposed solutions. Some of their demands also overlap with left-wing politics, liberalism, or regional autonomy. Han nationalism therefore cannot simply be equated with nationalism in the conventional right-wing sense. Its internal political demands in fact reflect real tensions in Chinese society concerning employment, working conditions, fiscal pressure, regional governance, population decline, marriage and fertility, and cultural identity. This article does not attempt to estimate the actual social size of these tendencies. Instead, it treats the five categories as analytical ideal types for understanding internal differences within Chinese Internet Han nationalism in the 2020s.

articles.title: Organisational Knowledge Brokerage in Science Diplomacy: The Making of AI Governance at UNESCO and the European Union
articles.authors: Adam McCarthy, Alice Naisbitt, Pedro Dos Santos Maia, Barbara Riberio, Kieron Flanagan, Philip Shapira

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: We examine how expertise, evidence and authority are organised in the international governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and what this reveals about the practice of science diplomacy. Science-diplomacy scholarship has become increasingly attentive to the political character of expertise and to the ways knowledge is mobilised within international governance. Yet less attention has been paid to the organisational practices through which such knowledge is brokered within governance processes. Drawing on documentary analysis and 23 semi-structured interviews, we compare UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and the EU AI Act. Through an abductive analysis, we develop Organisational Knowledge Brokerage (OKB) to explain how a contested object such as AI is made workable for governance. We identify four connected practices through which this occurs: stabilising the governance object, legitimising expertise, building authority and operationalising governance. These practices took different forms under contrasting institutional mandates and governing capacities. UNESCO worked through global intergovernmental standard-setting and implementation support, while the EU combined supranational regulation with expert advice and Member State coordination. Across both cases, OKB also produced a cross-cutting process that we term normative translation, through which contested values acquired practical meaning in definitions, assessments and procedures. We show how this brokerage allowed each organisation to establish workable and revisable settlements around AI under conditions of technological uncertainty and dispersed authority. The article therefore develops a practice-oriented account of science diplomacy as organisational work through which knowledge, values and institutional authority are assembled for collective action in international technology governance.
